data.note:
Unblinded dossier – s_3069b9414e was **simvastatin**.

**Identity & annotated MoA:** PubChem CID 54454, simvastatin (Zocor, MK-733, Synvinolin), C25H38O5, structure verified as name and BBBC021 structure agree (e21). ChEMBL CHEMBL1064, max phase 4, mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (CHEMBL402, SINGLE PROTEIN) – consistent with BBBC021 Cholesterol-lowering class (e21).

Simvastatin is a classic HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor for cholesterol lowering (PMID 30422514; PMID 32729746 overview statin pharmacology). Inhibition depletes mevalonate → loss of isoprenoid prenylation of Rho/Rac GTPases, causing actin cytoskeleton rearrangement and altered cell morphology (PMID 30009811 simvastatin-dependent actin cytoskeleton rearrangement).

**What I did:** At 0.6µM saw frac_large_nucleus z+9.96 and cell enlargement, at 6µM frac_mitotic_like z+12.1, tub/act texture increase, irregular protrusive cells. Microscopist suggested Aurora kinase inhibitors biphasic polyploidy→mitotic arrest; I submitted Aurora p=0.58 then revised to 0.38 after PI critique.

**What was true:** NSC over 4 wells was 2-2 tie Aurora vs Cholesterol-lowering (summed sim 1.374 vs 1.637, e8) with 8/10 k-neighbours Epithelial and top neighbours mevinolin/lovastatin (other statins) sim 0.716→0.686. Per-dose dose-responses were n=1 with p≈0.2-0.6.

**Why I was wrong:** 
- Over-weighted single-replicate low-dose large-nucleus signal: 0.6µM had only 61 cells, frac_large_nucleus 0.02 ≈1 cell, no multinucleate increase (z-1.89), yet I treated as robust polyploidy hallmark separating Aurora from Eg5/Cholesterol.
- Ignored NSC prior: I moved away from tie on basis of striking images/features despite instruction that low similarity/ split vote = weak evidence and need multiple independent results.
- Ignored reviewer fragility: dose trends for frac_large_nucleus, cell_area, nuc_dna_integrated all p>0.2 and non-monotonic; cell_count flat (r=-0.4) argued against true mitotic toxicity.
- Missed atlas clue: nearest referen

reflection.text: After unblinding this was scored INCORRECT: submitted Aurora kinase inhibitors (final p=0.38, initial p=0.58) vs truth Cholesterol-lowering - simvastatin, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. PubChem CID 54454 and ChEMBL CHEMBL1064 agree name and BBBC021 structure agree per e20/e21, mechanism HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor INHIBITOR of CHEMBL402 e20. This matches literature found in this run for simvastatin e22/e23, including PMID 30422514 and the broader statin interaction literature PMID 32729746.
what_was_right: Atlas signal correctly flagged truth early but was discounted: First compare_to_reference_atlas over 2 wells e5 was NSC 1/2 Aurora but k-neighbours were Cholesterol-lowering 3/10, Actin disruptors 2/10, Eg5 2/10. Final atlas over 4 wells e8 was NSC 2/4 Cholesterol-lowering (summed similarity 1.637 vs Aurora 1.374 per review) with k-neighbours Epithelial 8/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10. In update_hypotheses step 12 we kept Aurora 0.58 and Cholesterol-lowering 0.18 despite this tie, and in step 18 we kept Aurora 0.38 vs Cholesterol-lowering 0.24 - over-calibrated toward Aurora.

Microscopist e4 was correctly uncertain: 'density lower vs DMSO; 16 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, Eg5 inhibitors, unknown' - i.e. could not exclude Eg5/microtubule. We treated this as support for Aurora in e12/e13 rather than as uncertainty.

High-dose phenotype e3 w_4c68b3dbce dose 6, 6 uM frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1, cell_roundness z=-11.4, cell_area z=-10.2 and intermediate e6 w_d8b83f4cfe dose 5, 2 uM cell_area z=-8.8, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-6.5 is real statin-induced morphology change, not mitotic arrest. PMID 30009811 returned by e23 shows simvastatin-dependent actin cytoskeleton rearrangement regulates differentiation via ERK1/2 and p38 - a documented pleiotropic morphology effect that can mimic mitotic-like shrinkage/rounding in Cell Painting, without Aurora activity. We read it as mitotic arrest.

Dose-response statistics correctly warned us fragility: e9 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e10 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 p=0.2, e11 cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e14 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e15 cell_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e16 frac_multinucleate rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e17 nuc_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2. All n=4 wells, n=1 per dose, all p>0.2, not significant. We still used rho=-0.80/ +0.80 as 'biphasic hallmark of Aurora' in rationale for e12.
what_was_wrong: The discriminating Aurora feature was low-dose large-nucleus/polyploidy: e2 w_6d94986897 dose 4 0.6 uM frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, cell_major_axis z=+5.3, cell_area z=+5.0 with only 61 cells measured, and e7 w_695807293b dose 3 0.2 uM frac_large_nucleus z=+6.9, frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+4.9. The review correctly flagged this as fragile: 0.6 uM frac_large_nucleus 0.02 is ~1 cell in n=61, no consistent buccal/multinucleate increase, no nuc_dna_integrated increase replication. We did not have replication because we exhausted budget: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.006-20 uM, 4 of 4 wells left e1, and we sampled 0.6 uM, 6 uM, 2 uM, 0.2 uM e2,e3,e6,e7 spending all 4 wells. Dose 4 0.6 uM was thus n=1.

Acquisition choice prioritized spread across doses to chase biphasic pattern instead of replication. The requested_experiment after first submit was explicit: acquire one replicate well at dose index 4 (0.6 uM) replicate 2 and test whether frac_large_nucleus, nuc_dna_integrated and cell enlargement reproduce e12 review critique. We logged in e18/e19 that we could not acquire due to 0/4 budget and tried to compensate with additional dose_response calculations e14-e17, which all returned non-significant p=0.6/0.2 and actually contradicted sustained polyploidy (nuc_area rho=-0.80, nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40). We downgraded from 0.58 to 0.38 but left Aurora on top instead of falling below Cholesterol/Eg5 as review instructed.

Cell enlargement vs shrinkage was inconsistent and we ignored contradiction: e2 showed enlargement at 0.6 uM but e6 at 2 uM and e3 at 6 uM showed strong shrinkage (cell_area z=-8.8 and -10.2). True dose-response for cell_area was negative rho=-0.80 e15, nuc_area rho=-0.80 e17, not the enlargement expected for stable endoreduplication. We rationalized this as biphasic Aurora (small-dose polyploidy, high-dose arrest) rather than toxicity / actin collapse expected for statins.

Weighting error: we gave more weight to microscopist candidate list and high z-scores (|z|>5-12) than to atlas summed similarity and k-neighbour prevalence. Epithelial 8/10 neighbours in e8 should have prompted stronger consideration that cholesterol-lowering actin/membrane phenotype was projecting to epithelial-like neighbors, not Aurora.

citations.claim: simvastatin is HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor / cholesterol-lowering mechanism verified post-unblinding
simvastatin-dependent actin cytoskeleton rearrangement can produce morphology changes that mimic mitotic phenotypes in this assay

reflection.next_experiment: As flagged in review: replicate dose 4 0.6 uM rep2 with adequate cell count >200 to test replication of frac_large_nucleus and nuc_dna_integrated z. Only if reproduced, proceed to phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 / phospho-Aurora immunofluorescence plus DNA-content flow cytometry and tubulin spindle imaging with Aurora inhibitor positive control to separate true cytokinesis failure from statin actin/roundness artefact. Atlas prior should be weighted by summed similarity and k-neighbours, not just NSC vote, when n=1 p>0.2.

## Reflection

After unblinding this was scored INCORRECT: submitted Aurora kinase inhibitors (final p=0.38, initial p=0.58) vs truth Cholesterol-lowering - simvastatin, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. PubChem CID 54454 and ChEMBL CHEMBL1064 agree name and BBBC021 structure agree per e20/e21, mechanism HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor INHIBITOR of CHEMBL402 e20. This matches literature found in this run for simvastatin e22/e23, including PMID 30422514 and the broader statin interaction literature PMID 32729746.

What was right:
- Atlas signal correctly flagged truth early but was discounted: First compare_to_reference_atlas over 2 wells e5 was NSC 1/2 Aurora but k-neighbours were Cholesterol-lowering 3/10, Actin disruptors 2/10, Eg5 2/10. Final atlas over 4 wells e8 was NSC 2/4 Cholesterol-lowering (summed similarity 1.637 vs Aurora 1.374 per review) with k-neighbours Epithelial 8/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10. In update_hypotheses step 12 we kept Aurora 0.58 and Cholesterol-lowering 0.18 despite this tie, and in step 18 we kept Aurora 0.38 vs Cholesterol-lowering 0.24 - over-calibrated toward Aurora.
- Microscopist e4 was correctly uncertain: 'density lower vs DMSO; 16 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, Eg5 inhibitors, unknown' - i.e. could not exclude Eg5/microtubule. We treated this as support for Aurora in e12/e13 rather than as uncertainty.
- High-dose phenotype e3 w_4c68b3dbce dose 6, 6 uM frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1, cell_roundness z=-11.4, cell_area z=-10.2 and intermediate e6 w_d8b83f4cfe dose 5, 2 uM cell_area z=-8.8, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-6.5 is real statin-induced morphology change, not mitotic arrest. PMID 30009811 returned by e23 shows simvastatin-dependent actin cytoskeleton rearrangement regulates differentiation via ERK1/2 and p38 - a documented pleiotropic morphology effect that can mimic mitotic-like shrinkage/rounding in Cell Painting, without Aurora activity. We read it as mitotic arrest.
- Dose-response statistics correctly warned us fragility: e9 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e10 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 p=0.2, e11 cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e14 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e15 cell_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e16 frac_multinucleate rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e17 nuc_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2. All n=4 wells, n=1 per dose, all p>0.2, not significant. We still used rho=-0.80/ +0.80 as 'biphasic hallmark of Aurora' in rationale for e12.

What was wrong or missed:
- The discriminating Aurora feature was low-dose large-nucleus/polyploidy: e2 w_6d94986897 dose 4 0.6 uM frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, cell_major_axis z=+5.3, cell_area z=+5.0 with only 61 cells measured, and e7 w_695807293b dose 3 0.2 uM frac_large_nucleus z=+6.9, frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+4.9. The review correctly flagged this as fragile: 0.6 uM frac_large_nucleus 0.02 is ~1 cell in n=61, no consistent buccal/multinucleate increase, no nuc_dna_integrated increase replication. We did not have replication because we exhausted budget: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.006-20 uM, 4 of 4 wells left e1, and we sampled 0.6 uM, 6 uM, 2 uM, 0.2 uM e2,e3,e6,e7 spending all 4 wells. Dose 4 0.6 uM was thus n=1.
- Acquisition choice prioritized spread across doses to chase biphasic pattern instead of replication. The requested_experiment after first submit was explicit: acquire one replicate well at dose index 4 (0.6 uM) replicate 2 and test whether frac_large_nucleus, nuc_dna_integrated and cell enlargement reproduce e12 review critique. We logged in e18/e19 that we could not acquire due to 0/4 budget and tried to compensate with additional dose_response calculations e14-e17, which all returned non-significant p=0.6/0.2 and actually contradicted sustained polyploidy (nuc_area rho=-0.80, nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40). We downgraded from 0.58 to 0.38 but left Aurora on top instead of falling below Cholesterol/Eg5 as review instructed.
- Cell enlargement vs shrinkage was inconsistent and we ignored contradiction: e2 showed enlargement at 0.6 uM but e6 at 2 uM and e3 at 6 uM showed strong shrinkage (cell_area z=-8.8 and -10.2). True dose-response for cell_area was negative rho=-0.80 e15, nuc_area rho=-0.80 e17, not the enlargement expected for stable endoreduplication. We rationalized this as biphasic Aurora (small-dose polyploidy, high-dose arrest) rather than toxicity / actin collapse expected for statins.
- Weighting error: we gave more weight to microscopist candidate list and high z-scores (|z|>5-12) than to atlas summed similarity and k-neighbour prevalence. Epithelial 8/10 neighbours in e8 should have prompted stronger consideration that cholesterol-lowering actin/membrane phenotype was projecting to epithelial-like neighbors, not Aurora.

Proposed next experiment: As flagged in review: replicate dose 4 0.6 uM rep2 with adequate cell count >200 to test replication of frac_large_nucleus and nuc_dna_integrated z. Only if reproduced, proceed to phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 / phospho-Aurora immunofluorescence plus DNA-content flow cytometry and tubulin spindle imaging with Aurora inhibitor positive control to separate true cytokinesis failure from statin actin/roundness artefact. Atlas prior should be weighted by summed similarity and k-neighbours, not just NSC vote, when n=1 p>0.2.
